lesson.title: The Short Ball Is Not Permission
lesson.hook: A short ball pulls you forward. Its height decides what it earns: the open court, or an approach.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time a ball lands short, check its height first: high, take the open court; low, lift an approach and come in.

pro.label: Nadal, Monte Carlo 2017 final
pro.moment: Nadal aimed his heavy forehand at Ramos-Vinolas's backhand to create space, and was quick to move up the court for the short ball.
pro.read: The attack begins one ball before the short ball.

drill.name: Earned or not
drill.how: Rally. Any ball that lands inside your service line: above net height and balanced, attack the open court; below it, lift a deep approach and come in. Never flat from below the net. Your partner calls "earned" or "approach" after each one.

lesson.cue: High: go. Low: lift and come in.

steps.name: The short slice
steps.sit: Their slice lands short and stays low. You come forward to it; they're still deep.
steps.q: How hard do you go at this one?
opts: High through the middle, stay back
Lift an approach and come in
steps.payoff: Balanced but low: approach and come in, rather than go for the winner.
steps.principle: Low contact means lift and margin. Their deep position still invites you forward.
steps.why: The slice stays below the net, so a flat drive has no room. You've already come forward: lift a deep approach and keep coming, rather than stopping mid-court.

lines.A: Flat from below the net — into the tape.
lines.B: Too safe — you're caught mid-court, and their deep ball rushes you.
lines.C: Lift it, come in — their pass is yours to volley.
lines.D: Low and flat from below the net — it finds the tape.

steps.take: Balanced but low: approach with lift — don't go for the winner.

steps.name: The waist-high ball
steps.sit: Now the ball sits waist-high. You're set, and they're stranded out wide.
steps.q: What does this ball let you do?
opts: Drive it at them, then come in
steps.payoff: Waist-high, set, and they're stranded: now the attack is earned.
steps.principle: Short is an invitation. Height, balance and their position decide if you accept.
steps.why: Everything lines up: a comfortable height, your feet set, and open court. Aim well inside the lines and come in behind it; you don't need a winner.

lines.A: They scramble; you come in and put it away.
lines.B: Straight to them — they're set, and the rally goes on.
lines.C: It lands this time, but only 5 in 10 do.
lines.D: Too safe — they recover and the point starts again.

steps.take: High, balanced, opponent stranded: attack — with margin.

steps.name: The short slice, backhand
steps.sit: Another short, low slice, this time to your backhand. They're deep again.
opts: Lift an approach and come in
High through the middle, stay back
steps.payoff: Other wing, same ball: lift it and come in.
steps.principle: The height decides, not the wing.
steps.why: The slice stays below the net, so a flat drive has no room. You've already come forward: lift a deep approach and keep coming, rather than stopping mid-court.

lines.A: Flat from below the net — into the tape.
lines.B: Lift it, come in — their pass is yours to volley.
lines.C: Too safe — you're caught mid-court, and their deep ball rushes you.
lines.D: Low and flat from below the net — it finds the tape.

steps.take: Short and low, either wing: lift a deep approach and come in.
